chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Muqri', from al-Muqani'i, from Bakkar, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sa'eed al-Asadi, from (his father), from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).
He said: In the year of the conquest, the Euphrates will split until it enters the streets of Kufa.

key_terms.الْفَتْح: The Conquest (referring to the conquest of Mecca or the final conquest by Imam Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Euphrates splitting in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifies the recession of the Euphrates as a specific eschatological sign occurring in the year of the Great Conquest (Fath), linking it to the emergence of hidden treasures and the expansion of Kufa's urban reach. In Shia scholarly tradition, this event is often interpreted not merely as a physical phenomenon but as a precursor to the rise of the Sufyani and the subsequent military campaigns that characterize the end times.
